newsitem.title: BRAZIL: TENNIS-WASHINGTON RESCUES U.S. IN BRAZIL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WASHINGTON RESCUES U.S. IN BRAZIL.

text.p: The United States had to survive an early scare before winning the opening rubber of their Davis Cup world group first round tie against Brazil on Friday.
Malivai Washington, called up to replace the injured Andre Agassi, lost the first set to Brazil's Gustavo Kuerten and had two set points against him in the tie-break at the end of the second.
But Washington saved both points, then went on to win the tie-break 8-6 and the match 3-6 7-6 7-6 6-3 in three hours and ten minutes.
The 1996 Wimbledon finalist, sixty-one places above his opponent in the world rankings, began nervously, making a series of unforced errors early on, but improved steadily as the game progressed.
Washington also had two set points against him in the tenth game of the third set but saved those as well, silencing the samba drums in a 4,000 crowd which was noisy but not badly behaved.
"I had several chances but didn't taken them," said Kuerten. "I played the same standard throughout but he got better as the match went on, that's why he won."
